sentences.text:
In this appeal, the 3rd respondent/Insurance Company has challenged the judgment and award dated 19.8.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.699/2013 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and C.J.M., and Additional MACT-VII at Shivamogga ('the Tribunal' in short).
2.
The appellant was respondent No.3, respondent No.1 was the petitioner, respondent No.2 was respondent No.1 and respondent No.3 was respondent No.2 before the Tribunal.
Rank of the parties will be referred to as per NC: 2024:KHC:1812 their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Briefly stated the facts are, on 24.04.2013 the appellant met with an accident while riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA-14/ED-9548 as a pillion rider, hit by a lorry bearing regn.No.KA-18/B-1757 injuring him at Muduba Grama on Umblebylu-Hanagere Temple road.
After taking treatment he approached the Tribunal for a grant of compensation of Rs.15,20,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the respondents.
The Tribunal, after taking evidence by impugned judgment awarded Rs.12,50,000/- with 6% interest per annum.
Aggrieved by the award, the Insurance Company has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.B.C.Shivanne Gowda, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Ms.Priyanka, learned counsel for the petitioner.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the accident took place on 24.04.2013, the petitioner is an agriculturalist, with no proof of income, his income ought to have been assessed as Rs.8,000/- but the Tribunal has assessed as RS.10,000/- in excess.
It is contended that the Tribunal has taken future prospects at 50% instead of 40% settled in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The compensation assessed being higher seeks for modification.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the petitioner has suffered fracture of right femur, fracture of calcaneum, fracture of right tibia and fibula with vascular injury.
He was under hospitalization for 57 days.

Due to vascular injury, his right lower limb was amputated and being an agriculturist, the Tribunal ought to have taken 100% functional disability for whole (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC:1812 body, but has assessed at 30% which is lower.
The income assessed is not proper, compensation assessed is meagre, he wants this Court to exercise its discretion to enhance the compensation and sought for higher compensation.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on both sides and perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident and injury sustained by the petitioner.
The medical record points out that the multiple fracture sustained by the petitioner with vascular injury to Tibia and Fibula, resulting in amputation of his right lower limb below knee.
The Medical Officer speaks of 70% right lower limb disability but the Tribunal has assessed at 30%.

Even in the absence of the medical evidence, the Tribunal ought to have placed reliance on Schedule-I of the Workmen's Compensation Act wherein part-II at Sl.No.20 and 21, the percentage of disability is fixed at 50% for NC: 2024:KHC:1812 amputation below knee.
Hence, 50% ought to have been taken as the permanent disability having regard to the petitioner being an agriculturist lost his active participation in agricultural supervision.

The medical evidence points out that the petitioner was under hospitalization from 24.4.2013 to 26.4.2013 at KMC, Manipal, 27.4.2013 to 27.05.2013 at JC Hospital Thirthahalli and he was in Father Muller Medical College Hospital, Mangalore from 13.6.2013 to 5.7.2013 in all 57 days.
9.

entities.text: Father Muller Medical College Hospital, Mangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Ex.P-7 is the RTC indicating that the petitioner is an agriculturalist, aged 39 years.
No doubt a person with no proof of income in the year 2013 will earn not less than Rs.8,000/-.
Rs.10,000/- is assessed by the Tribunal, hence the income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.8,000/-.

In view of the principles laid down in Pranay Sethi's case which is applicable in case of this nature for assessing loss of future prospects, 40% to be added for a person aged below 40 but the Tribunal has taken 50% on the higher side.
Hence, keeping all these aspects into consideration, the compensation has to be assessed.

sentences.text: In view of the medical evidence, future medical expense has to be assessed at Rs.25,000/-.
The petitioner was laid down for six months and loss of income for six months is Rs.48,000/-.
Loss of future income on account of permanent disability will be Rs.8,000/- + Rs.3,200/- (40% of future prospects) = Rs.11,200/- x 12 x 15 x 50% = Rs.10,08,000/-.

The petitioner is entitled to the compensation as follows;
1 Pain and suffering Rs.80,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs.1,80,000/-
3 Attendant charges Rs.15,200/-
(57 days x Rs.8,000/- pm)
4 Food and nourishment Rs.10,000/-

5 Travelling expenses Rs.10,000/-, 6 Loss of amenities and Rs.60,000/-
discomforts

7 Future Medical Expenses Rs.25,000/- 8 Loss of income during laid Rs.48,000/-
up period 9 Loss of Future Income Rs.10,08,000/-
The petitioner is entitled to Rs.14,36,200/- as against Rs.12,50,000/-.
Since the petitioner has not filed any appeal, it is not proper exercise discretion to enhance the compensation.
The Tribunal has given cogent reasoning in assessing the compensation which calls any interference.
The appeal is devoid of merits, in the result, the following:

ORDER (i) The appeal is dismissed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award is confirmed.

(iii) The insurance company is directed to satisfy the award, if not deposited already,
within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
